description: QSFSG (芪参芙参颗) formula for NAFLD / Liver Injury / abnormal lipid metabolism

supplement_references: Hu M, Yu Z, Wang J, et al. Traditional Uses, Origins, Chemistry and Pharmacology of Bombyx batryticatus: A Review. Molecules. 2017;22(10):1779. doi:10.3390/molecules22101779. PMID: 29053625; PMC: PMC6151799. — Comprehensive review listing flavonoids (quercetin, kaempferol), sterols (β-sitosterol, stigmasterol, daucosterol, ergostane derivatives), nucleosides (adenosine, uridine, adenine, hypoxanthine, xanthine), peptides (BB octapeptide, beauvericin, cyclic dipeptides) and amides (nicotinamide, aurantiamide) as documented constituents.

Liu et al. Discovery of antiepileptic Q-Markers for Bombyx batryticatus: Integrating serum pharmacochemistry, network pharmacology and temporal-efficacy validation. J Ethnopharmacol. 2025; doi:10.1016/j.jep.2025. — Identified beauvericin (192.3 µg/g), bassianolide (325.6 µg/g), and ammonium oxalate (66515 µg/g) as quality markers for antiepileptic effect.

Wang et al. Anticonvulsant Activity of Bombyx batryticatus and Analysis of Bioactive Extracts Based on UHPLC-Q-TOF MS/MS and Molecular Networking. Front Pharmacol. 2022. PMC: PMC9740854. — UHPLC-Q-TOF/MS analysis identified 65 compounds in Bombyx batryticatus extract.

Dong H, Ren JX, Wang JJ, et al. Chinese Medicinal Leech: Ethnopharmacology, Phytochemistry, and Pharmacological Activities. Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine. 2016; doi:10.1155/2016/7895935. — Comprehensive review of phytochemistry of Hirudo / Whitmania pigra reporting >51 small-molecule constituents including pteridines, sterols (β-sitosterol, stigmasterol, cholesterol, daucosterol), squalene, fatty acids, organic acids and bioactive peptides.

Chen et al. A Comprehensive Quality Evaluation System for Medicinal Leeches by Integrating Macromolecular Protein Analysis and Small-Molecule Marker Detection. Pharmaceuticals. 2025;18(6):887. PMC: PMC12195895. — Identified 13 small-molecule quality markers including 6 pteridines (Hirudinoidine A/B/C, Whitmanine B, Poecilobdellasulfide B, SZ-1), 3 nucleosides (inosine, hypoxanthine, xanthine), 3 amino acids (leucine, phenylalanine, tryptophan), and 1 piperidine (2-piperidone).

Zhang et al. Antithrombotic pharmacodynamics and metabolomics study in raw and processed products of Whitmania pigra Whitman. PMC: PMC11002550. — Metabolomics study identifying 66 differential metabolites including sphinganine, phosphorylcholine, arachidoyl ethanolamide and amino-acid derivatives.

Note: hirudin and hirudin-like peptide factors are the principal antithrombotic agents of medicinal leech but are large peptides (≈ 7 kDa) and therefore outside the small-molecule scope of this network-pharmacology pipeline (Müller et al., J Thromb Haemost 2022, doi:10.1111/jth.15762).
